Name: Sham Shui Po
Location: Around Sham Shui Po MTR, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Dense, lived-in district of fabric, button, leather and paper wholesalers, electronics stalls, old-school eateries and a growing set of indie shops. Why: The most authentic everyday-and-craft shopping neighbourhood in Kowloon, and good for street photography.

Name: To Kwa Wan and the 13 Streets
Location: Between Kowloon City Road, To Kwa Wan Road, Mok Cheong Street and Ma Tau Kok Road, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Grid of short parallel streets lined with late-1950s buildings, named after auspicious creatures like dragon, phoenix and crane, with small shops and cafes. Why: A quiet, textured old-Kowloon grid that few visitors see; pair with the nearby waterfront (Kowloon City Pier, Hoi Sham Park).

Name: Kennedy Town
Location: Forbes Street, Kennedy Town, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Western end of the Island line with cafes along Forbes Street, a harbourfront and the Sai Wan Swimming Shed, the last such shed on the waterfront. Why: A calmer, still-local side of the Island; iDiscover offers a free self-guided memory trail.

Name: Tai Hang
Location: Wun Sha Street and Lin Fa Temple area, Tai Hang, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Former village tucked behind Causeway Bay with indie cafes, small shops, Lin Fa Temple and the Tai Hang Fire Dragon Heritage Centre at 12 School Street. Why: Known for its Mid-Autumn Fire Dragon Dance and a cafe-and-shophouse stroll; the heritage centre shows the tradition year-round.

Name: Sai Ying Pun
Location: Second Street and Centre Street, Sai Ying Pun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hillside grid of early-developed streets (First, Second, Third, High) with cafes, restaurants, Sai Ying Pun Market at 44-45 Centre Street and the Centre Street escalator link. Why: Old Hong Kong grid with newer cafes and wine bars; steep, photogenic and close to Sheung Wan.

Name: Kwun Tong
Location: Hung To Road and Kwun Tong Promenade, Kwun Tong, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Former factory district whose industrial buildings now host studios, cafes and small restaurants, with a roughly 1 km waterfront promenade facing the Kai Tak cruise terminal. Why: A very different, utilitarian-creative Hong Kong; the promenade gives night views toward Hong Kong Island East.

Name: Quarry Bay and Tai Koo
Location: King's Road near Yick Cheong Building, Quarry Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Home of the Monster Building (an E-shaped 1960s housing complex of five connected blocks) and Taikoo Place's Sunday market on Tong Chong Street. Why: Iconic dense-housing photography; shoot from the street only, since the inner courtyard is now closed to the public.

Name: Yau Ma Tei
Location: Temple Street, Shanghai Street and Reclamation Street, Yau Ma Tei, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Old Kowloon quarter with the Tin Hau Temple, Shanghai Street's cookware and craft shops, the Jade Market and the 1913 wholesale fruit market (Grade II) on Reclamation Street. Why: Concentrated old-Kowloon life; the fruit market works overnight to morning, so visit respectfully.

Name: Tai O
Location: Kat Hing Street and the creek, Tai O, Lantau, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Fishing village on west Lantau with stilt houses, a small dried-seafood market and shops selling shrimp paste, salted fish and dried shrimp. The Tai O Heritage Hotel is a converted 1902 police station. Why: The best place to buy the village's signature shrimp paste and salted fish; Yik Cheong is a well-known shop and Ha Chu Beng on Kat Hing Street serves pancakes cooked with the local paste.

Name: Sheung Wan
Location: Wing Lok Street / Hollywood Road, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: One of the city's oldest districts: dried-seafood shops on Wing Lok Street, antique and gallery shops along Hollywood Road, Man Mo Temple, steep Ladder Street, and street art and indie shops around Tai Ping Shan Street. Why: Old Chinese trades and new design side by side on foot; works as a walking spine from Wing Lok Street up to Man Mo Temple and Tai Ping Shan.

Name: Kowloon City
Location: Nga Tsin Long Road / Kai Tak Road area, Kowloon City, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A former walled-city and airport-neighbour district known as Hong Kong's Little Thailand, with Thai restaurants and grocers, Kowloon Walled City Park, the Kowloon City market cooked food centre with dai pai dong upstairs, and old tong lau streets. Why: The best neighbourhood for a Thai-Chiu Chow food crawl and for old-Kai-Tak texture; reached by Sung Wong Toi or Kai Tak MTR.

Name: Mong Kok
Location: Nathan Road / Tung Choi Street, Mong Kok, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Dense market district: Ladies' Market on Tung Choi Street, Goldfish Street, Fa Yuen Street sneaker shops, Flower Market Road and Yuen Po Street Bird Garden, with street snacks throughout. Why: The most concentrated street-market energy in the city, busy late; combine a morning bird-garden/flower-market walk with an evening market run.

Name: Central and SoHo
Location: Queen's Road Central / Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The commercial and historic heart of Hong Kong Island: skyscrapers, Statue Square, Tai Kwun and PMQ on the north slope, and SoHo's restaurant and bar streets climbing the hill above Hollywood Road. Why: Contrasts heritage (Man Mo Temple, antique shops on Hollywood Road) with high-end dining and nightlife; the Mid-Levels Escalator links it all, and WinterFest lights and Christmas Town are typically in Statue Square.

Name: Wan Chai
Location: Johnston Road / Queen's Road East, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A layered district: the wet market and tong lau on Queen's Road East and Stone Nullah Lane (Blue House), the redeveloped Lee Tung Avenue ('Wedding Card Street'), Hennessy Road trams, and the Lockhart Road bar strip. Why: Old and new Hong Kong side by side, with early-morning markets, some of the city's best cheap eats, nightlife and heritage within a few blocks.

Name: Causeway Bay
Location: Hennessy Road / Yee Wo Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hong Kong Island's mass-market shopping and dining hub, with Sogo, Times Square, Lee Garden and Hysan malls, Jardine's Bazaar and Jardine's Crescent street stalls, Victoria Park, the Noon Day Gun and the villain-hitting spot at the Canal Road Flyover. Why: The densest retail crowd in Hong Kong, with Christmas displays and a street-level, local feel in the back lanes.

Name: Tsim Sha Tsui
Location: Nathan Road / Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Kowloon's southern tip and tourist heart: the harbourfront promenade and Avenue of Stars, museums and Cultural Centre, Kowloon Park, Chungking Mansions, tailors and Nathan Road's 'Golden Mile', plus Knutsford Terrace bars. Why: Home to the classic skyline view and Star Ferry, and one of the busiest Christmas-light zones.

Name: Sai Kung Town
Location: Sai Kung Public Pier and waterfront (Hoi Pong Street), Sai Kung Town, New Territories, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A laid-back fishing town and expat favourite on the Sai Kung peninsula, with a waterfront promenade nicknamed Seafood Street (live tanks, choose-your-own fish), the Old Town lanes, speedboats from the public pier to beaches and islands, and the gateway to the Geopark and hiking trails. Why: The quickest way to feel Hong Kong's coastal 'back garden', and the base for hikes such as Sharp Peak and Tai Long Wan.
